question: If a pair of linear equations is consistent, then the lines will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A **consistent** system of equations means there is **at least one solution**.

**Intersecting lines** provide exactly **one solution** (unique).

**Coincident lines** provide **infinitely many solutions**.

Since both cases yield solutions, a consistent pair must be **intersecting or coincident**.

**∴ The correct answer is intersecting or coincident.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A pair of linear equations is **consistent**.

Consider the general form: a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0.

A system is **consistent** if it has **one or more solutions**.

⇒ Case 1: **Unique Solution** (Intersecting Lines)

⇒ Condition: a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂

⇒ Case 2: **Infinite Solutions** (Coincident Lines)

⇒ Condition: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

⇒ If the system is **inconsistent**, it has **no solution** (Parallel Lines).

⇒ Condition: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂

**∴ The correct answer is intersecting or coincident.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inconsistent System

A pair of linear equations with no solution is called **inconsistent**, representing **parallel lines**.

Dependent Equations

A pair of **dependent** linear equations is always **consistent** and has infinitely many solutions (coincident lines).</p
